forward.candidate_a_coverage: A covers card reward options and MCC-dependent software/operations treatment plus review steps, but shows no evidence on opening eligibility or approving a new $100,000 charge.
forward.candidate_b_coverage: B covers high-limit application eligibility and documentation plus one reward exclusion showing Apple is only 1% on Silver, but lacks broad product comparison or clear large-charge approval procedure.

reversed.candidate_a_coverage: A covers high-limit eligibility and underwriting well via D1-D3 plus an Apple exclusion and software-rate rule in D4/D6, but it lacks broad product comparison and clear procedures for a $100,000 first charge.
reversed.candidate_b_coverage: B covers rewards classification, rates, exclusions, posting/review procedures, and some transaction-limit evidence via D11/D12/D17 and D1, but its large-charge approval and underwriting support is thinner.

forward.candidate_a_coverage: A covers posting timing, returns reversals, card/category/promo recalculation, and some exclusions, but its followup evidence is mostly off-card/product and misses customer review or dispute steps.
forward.candidate_b_coverage: B covers posted eligibility, ineligible types, refunds/disputes, promo rules, and dispute/correction workflow, though some evidence is from mixed card products and omits transaction-level review details.

reversed.candidate_a_coverage: A covers posted-date accrual, returns/reversals, dispute correction steps, and some promo/category logic, but its best followup adds mostly mismatched card-product rules and misses clear transaction-level review/error procedures.
reversed.candidate_b_coverage: B covers posted-date accrual, exclusions, returns/credits, MCC/category-based rates, and dispute/correction workflow, though some followup evidence is from mismatched products and weak on account review specifics.
